subject: Post-demo: economic buyer, procurement path & systems-in-scope — action items
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: economic buyer, procurement path & systems-in-scope — action items

Hi Amit — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

1) Decision makers: you mentioned procurement (Lena) + finance/CFO (Priya) as the final approvers. Can you confirm who we should include on procurement emails and who will sign?

2) Security questionnaire: attached is a short Redwood Security Q&A (v1) — can your security team start this and flag questions we should sync on?

3) Systems in scope: from the call I heard ingestion API + embeddings storage + internal runtime for inference (no user-facing PII flows today). Please confirm if any additional systems (on-prem DBs, analytics pipelines) should be listed.

4) Timeline & procurement path: propose security Q completed by Aug 25, security sync (30–45 min) the week of Aug 31, procurement paperwork (SOW/PO) week of Sep 6. Is that realistic on your side?

Decision criteria we heard from you today (please correct/add): low-latency for inference, deterministic costs per 1M tokens, clear controls around data retention and KMS.

Attachments: Redwood_Security_QA_v1.pdf (pdf)

Next actions: can you confirm the economic buyer and procurement contact and loop them into this thread? If fine, I’ll add our security engineer and account lead for the sync.

Thanks — Tessa

--
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
Book time: https://cal.redwood.com/tessa

Tessa — thanks for the clear recap. A few notes from our side: 

- Economic buyer: Priya Nair (CFO) will sign off on spend >$200k. Priya copied below (I’ll bcc her on the procurement thread once we have an initial commercial).
- Procurement lead: Lena is the procurement owner — looping her in. Lena, we’re evaluating Redwood for customer-facing document ingestion and some internal analytics workflows.
- Security intake: attaching our initial network diagram and high-level environment overview so you have context. Our security team will start on your QA — they prefer to see SOC 2 Type II evidence and encryption-at-rest details up front.

Notes on scope: we do have one on-prem data store that may need to be considered if we pull historical customer records. I’ve flagged that for the security team; we’ll confirm whether that becomes in-scope.

Tentative timeline: Aug 25 for QA return sounds good; security call Sep 1 morning PT; procurement paperwork mid-Sep (we have an internal deadline around Sep 15 for vendor approvals).

Attachment: ledger_network_diagram.png (png)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Looping in security & AM: proposed plan and quick asks

Thanks — quick notes from security side after a first pass: 

- Scope confirmation: ingestion API, embeddings storage, and runtime for live inference are in-scope. The on-prem DB you mentioned will be "conditional scope" — if we touch PII or export data into embeddings, we’ll need to include it. Please confirm whether historical PII export is expected.
- SOC 2: we can share our last report and the control matrix.
- KMS / encryption: Redwood supports customer-managed keys (KMS) for Private deployments; for Hosted we offer envelope encryption with strict key rotation policies. Need ledger procurement/KMS owner contact for key provisioning.
- IP allowlist: please provide IP ranges or cloud egress endpoints so we can prepare allowlist instructions.

I attached a short security_req_checklist.xlsx to track outstanding items and owner assignments. I’ll take point on the SOC2 deliverables and the KMS questions.

Next: Amit / Lena — can you confirm whether the historical DB is in or out of scope and provide a KMS contact? If yes, we’ll move the security sync to a working session and include a short demo of our Private deployment options.

Attachment: security_req_checklist.xlsx (xlsx)
